circulars.subject_full: Listing of Equity Shares of Anawil Wire and Engineering Limited (SME IPO)

movers.headline: approves **two separate capacity expansions** at the board meeting of 07-Aug-2026, and they must be read apart because only one is the Company's own spend. First, it raises the total outlay on its **ongoing capacity expansion from Rs 550 cr to approximately Rs 617 cr**, enlarging the scope of capacity augmentation in the **Medium Voltage and High Voltage power cable** businesses through debottlenecking — an update to the plan it first disclosed on February 6, 2026, and at ~13.7% of a Rs 4,514 cr market cap the **largest own-balance-sheet capex on today's tape**. Second, and far larger, it approves tripling the optical fibre capacity of **Birla Furukawa Fibre Optics Private Limited** — a **joint venture** with Furukawa Electric Co, Japan, not a subsidiary — together with an upstream **'Preform'** manufacturing facility, at an **estimated aggregate outlay of approximately USD 500 million, which the filing itself equates to approximately Rs 4,800 cr**, funded by a mix of internal accrual, equity and debt and targeted for completion by **31-Dec-2028**. State the two caveats the company states: the figure is *subject to finer detailed engineering and other aspects of the project which are under evaluation*, and it is the **JV's** outlay, so Universal Cables' share of it is not disclosed here. Even discounted for both, Rs 4,800 cr against a Rs 4,514 cr market cap is the largest capital commitment on the tape by a wide margin. *(Missed by the original digest entirely: all six of the company's filings landed 21:43-23:41, after the 21:40 read cut-off, and were scraped the following day; the amount field was never populated because both figures sit inside the PDF, so the auto baseline scored it at zero.)*
movers.quantum: Rs 617 cr own cable outlay (from Rs 550 cr); plus ~USD 500 mn / ~Rs 4,800 cr at the JV

movers.headline: wins a **batch of offshore orders from the Oil & Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC)** for the **Pipeline Replacement Project (PRP-X) and the Well Head Platforms Project off India's west coast**, booked by L&T Energy Hydrocarbon Offshore. **Read the size the way L&T states it, because it never states a rupee value:** the press release classifies the win as **'Major'**, and the classification table printed at the foot of that same release defines Major as **Rs 5,000–10,000 cr** (Significant 1,000–2,500 · Large 2,500–5,000 · Major 5,000–10,000 · Mega 10,000–15,000 · Ultra-Mega >15,000). That band is the company's disclosure; the **~0.9–1.8% of a Rs 5,57,996 cr market cap is our arithmetic on the band**, not a figure L&T published. On the band's own terms this is the largest order on the tape today. *(Invisible to the auto baseline, which stored `amount_rs=0` because there is no rupee figure in the document to extract.)*
movers.quantum: Rs 5,000–10,000 cr (L&T's own 'Major' band); ~0.9–1.8% of mcap

movers.headline: **completes** the acquisition of **100% of Maruti Clean Coal & Power Limited (MCCPL)** from Kolahai Infotech Private Limited and SFI Parcel Services Private Limited, first signed 13-Jun-2026; MCCPL is now a wholly-owned subsidiary. The asset is a **300 MW thermal plant at Korba, Chhattisgarh**, and the filing values the transaction at an **enterprise value of Rs 1,410 cr** against the acquired asset's **FY26 EBITDA of ~Rs 279 cr** — so ~5x EBITDA, and the company calls it EBITDA- and PAT-accretive from day one. The offtake is contracted rather than merchant for most of it: a **195 MW (net) long-term PPA with Rajasthan discoms routed through PTC India with ~14 years of residual life**, 5% at variable cost to the Chhattisgarh discom, and only the balance ~64 MW sold merchant; coal is tied up under a long-term FSA with SECL plus SHAKTI linkage. Installed capacity goes to **14,835 MW**. At ~1.4% of a Rs 1,03,482 cr market cap it is small for JSW Energy — it is here because it is the **largest completed transaction on the tape**, and the money has actually moved.
movers.quantum: Rs 1,410.00 cr enterprise value; ~1.4% of mcap

movers.headline: approves a **capacity expansion at its Kuppam unit in Chitoor, Andhra Pradesh** — **existing capacity up to 20 kilo-tonnes per annum, running at 80–85% utilisation, with up to 10 KTPA to be added by FY2029**. The stated investment is **Rs 768 cr, explicitly excluding Rs 40 cr of Interest During Construction**, funded by internal accrual and debt, with the rationale given as growth and expansion. This is core capacity, not captive power, so it qualifies under CLAUDE.md §6, and it is the **largest rupee capex a company commits from its own balance sheet today**, behind only Universal Cables' JV-level optical-fibre outlay. Against a Rs 2,38,116 cr market cap it is ~0.3% — immaterial to the equity, material to the unit: a **50% capacity increase at a plant already running near full**. *(Recovered: the figure sits in the Regulation 30 disclosure table, so the baseline stored 0 and carried the row as an unquantified capex line.)*
movers.quantum: Rs 768.00 cr (+Rs 40 cr IDC); ~0.3% of mcap

movers.headline: approves **raising up to Rs 650 cr through a rights issue to existing shareholders**, with the proceeds earmarked for deleveraging and a stated ambition of being **debt-free by FY27**. **State the stage: this is board-approved and nothing more** — the terms that decide the dilution (issue price, rights entitlement ratio, record date, payment schedule) are all delegated to a newly constituted Securities Issuance Committee 'at a later date', and the enabling **increase in authorised share capital from Rs 101 cr to Rs 146 cr** still needs members' consent at the 40th AGM. What is not conditional is the scale: **~16.7% of a Rs 3,903 cr market cap**, the largest fresh-equity call on the tape today. *(The baseline typed this `equity_allotment` and flagged it as a content mismatch, holding a Rs 650 cr rights issue out of movers entirely; a rights issue approval is fresh equity, not an allotment.)*
movers.quantum: up to Rs 650.00 cr — approved, not raised; ~16.7% of mcap

movers.headline: **completes** a **Qualified Institutions Placement raising Rs 200 cr**, having **allotted 23,80,952 equity shares at an issue price of Rs 840 per share**. This is the rarest of today's raise rows — **money in the bank, not a ceiling or an authorisation**: the shares are allotted, the price is struck and the placement document's objects govern the use, which the company states as repayment or prepayment of certain outstanding borrowings, in part or full, plus general corporate purposes. At ~7.6% of a Rs 2,636 cr market cap the dilution is real and the stated purpose is balance-sheet repair rather than growth capex. *(The baseline filed it under Equity allotments and never promoted it; a QIP is fresh equity.)*
movers.quantum: Rs 200.00 cr — QIP completed and allotted; ~7.6% of mcap

movers.headline: approves a **capacity addition for the development of an Intermediate Block at an estimated capex of Rs 149 cr**. The disclosure is thin — the intimation gives the block and the number and not much else, with no commissioning date, financing mix or tonnage in the covering letter. Taken at face value it is core process capacity in the intermediates chain, so it qualifies under CLAUDE.md §6, and at ~2.4% of a Rs 6,218 cr market cap it is a **top-three rupee capex on the tape**. *(Recovered: the baseline carried this as an unquantified capex line — the Rs 149 cr sits past the covering letter and `amount_rs` stored 0.)*

approves a **preferential issue of up to 32,00,000 equity shares at Rs 375 each (face value Rs 5, premium Rs 370), aggregating up to Rs 120,00,00,125**, in one or more tranches. Two things distinguish it from the day's other raise approvals. First, the allottees span **both the Promoter & Promoter Group AND the Non-Promoter category** — promoters putting money in at a struck price, not just outside institutions. Second, it is **dated**: the board has convened an **Extraordinary General Meeting on 02-Sep-2026** to seek the members' approval, so unlike an open-ended enabling resolution there is a decision point on the calendar. It remains a **proposal until that vote and the other regulatory consents**. ~7.7% of a Rs 1,569 cr market cap.
movers.quantum: up to Rs 120.00 cr — approved, pending EGM 02-Sep-2026; ~7.7% of mcap

movers.headline: is **declared the successful bidder** for the **Development, Operation and Maintenance of the Multi Modal Logistics Park (MMLP) at Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh**, on a **Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer (DBFOT) public-private partnership** basis, awarded by Varanasi MMLP Limited. The annexure states the **broad consideration or size of the contract as Rs 91.60 cr**, a **construction period of 1 year from the appointed date and a concession period of 45 years including construction**. Read those two together before reading the number: a **45-year DBFOT concession is an operating asset the company funds and owns for four decades**, so Rs 91.60 cr is the disclosed contract consideration and not the lifetime economics of the park in either direction. It clears the CLAUDE.md §5 bar only barely, at ~1.1% of a Rs 8,425 cr market cap. **The award is a bid outcome — the filing records no concession agreement or LoA yet**, and the company undertakes to update on further developments.

approves a **preferential issue of up to 10,00,00,000 fully convertible warrants at Rs 8.60 per warrant, aggregating up to Rs 86,00,00,000**, for cash, to persons and entities in both the **Promoter & Promoter Group and the Public** category, subject to members' and regulatory approval. **The proportion is the story, not the rupees:** Rs 86 cr against a **Rs 219 cr market cap is ~39%**, and each warrant converts into one equity share of Re 1 face value — the largest proportional capital call on today's tape by a wide margin. It is a **proposal**: warrants are typically subscribed at 25% up front with the balance due on conversion, so even on approval the cash arrives in two stages and the dilution is deferred. *(Fully invisible to the auto baseline: the row was flagged as a content mismatch with `amount_rs=0` and appeared as a bare board-outcome line in Other notable.)*
movers.quantum: up to Rs 86.00 cr — approved, not raised; ~39.3% of mcap

movers.headline: **pays out Rs 60 cr as security deposit** under the **Letter of Intent dated 30-Jul-2026 from the Resolution Professional in the corporate insolvency resolution process of M/s Amzen Transportation Industries Private Limited** — i.e. Cosmic CRF is the successful resolution applicant for a corporate debtor. The filing itemises it: **Rs 28.40 cr as performance security deposit (10% of the amount payable to all stakeholders including CIRP costs), discharged by a bank guarantee issued 07-Aug**, and **Rs 31.60 cr paid on 06-Aug to the secured financial creditors, UCO Bank and Prudent ARC**. **The direction matters — this is money leaving the company**, and the Rs 60 cr is a deposit against a resolution plan, not the plan's total consideration, which the filing does not state. ~4.9% of a Rs 1,229 cr market cap. *(Recovered and re-typed: the baseline stored 0 and carried it in Order wins — an insolvency acquisition is not an order.)*

reports that its subsidiary **Vortex Engineering Private Limited has received a purchase order from one of India's largest public sector banks** for the **end-to-end supply, installation, commissioning and maintenance of 540 ATMs and 1 KVA UPS, including AMC, over a period of 5 years**, with a stated **contract value of Rs 37.79 cr**. Two qualifications belong in the same breath: the company calls it a **repeat order**, and the **customer is never named** — 'one of India's largest public sector banks' is as far as the disclosure goes, so counterparty concentration cannot be assessed. Spread over five years and inclusive of maintenance, the annual revenue content is a fraction of the headline. At ~5.8% of a Rs 649 cr market cap it is still the most material order of the day relative to size among the larger names. *(The baseline held this out of movers as a content mismatch and published it unquantified.)*

secures an **export order from SAMM Corporation, Delhi (a merchant exporter) for the manufacture and supply of railway parts to be used in the Russian Railways**. The filing splits the size across two years — **an aggregate order value of approximately Rs 8 cr for FY 2026-27 and approximately Rs 12 cr for FY 2027-28** — with immediate delivery and phased deliveries from August 2026. Note the structure: the awarding entity is **domestic** (SAMM), and the export to Russia is SAMM's leg, not KVS's, so the currency and country risk sit with the merchant exporter. Against a **Rs 123 cr market cap** the FY28 leg alone is ~9.8% and **the two legs together are ~16% — that combined figure is ours, summed from the filing's own two numbers, which it never adds up itself**. *(The baseline stored only the Rs 12 cr FY28 leg and published it as the order value.)*
movers.quantum: ~Rs 8.00 cr (FY27) + ~Rs 12.00 cr (FY28); ~9.8% of mcap on the FY28 leg

movers.headline: is awarded a contract by **Bimbo Bakeries India Private Limited** for the **construction of civil works and facilities at its manufacturing plant in Serkadu Village, Tamil Nadu**, which the company frames as a **re-entry into the Industrial & Utility Building segment**. The filing gives both figures and they are worth keeping apart: **basic value Rs 9,50,63,345 excluding GST, total purchase-order amount Rs 11,21,74,747 including applicable taxes**. Execution is **20 weeks**, payment 90% against RA bills within 15 days of certification with 10% released after a **1-year defect liability period** backed by a performance bank guarantee, and liquidated damages run at 0.5% a week capped at 10%. At ~6.4% of a Rs 148 cr market cap on the basic value it is a meaningful single order for the company. *(The baseline published the basic value alone as 'Rs 9.51 cr'.)*
movers.quantum: Rs 9.51 cr basic / Rs 11.22 cr incl taxes; ~6.4% of mcap

movers.headline: receives a purchase order for the **supply of plates plus frames for an electrical company**, of approximately **INR 3,68,18,597 excluding tax**, to be **executed by 27-Aug-2026** with payment within 30 days of the PO. The **counterparty is disclosed only as '*Domestic Company*'** — the filing names neither the customer nor the end product beyond that, which is the limit of what can be said about it. At ~1.9% of a Rs 199 cr market cap it clears the CLAUDE.md §5 bar, and the three-week execution window means it converts to revenue inside the current quarter.
movers.quantum: Rs 3.68 cr excl tax; ~1.9% of mcap

movers.headline: receives a work order from **Remal Alcast Private Limited** for **consultancy services on industrial plot acquisition and on the land-allotment process**, valued at **Rs 1,05,00,000 excluding GST at 18%**, payable 100% against completion of work and executable within 30 days of the purchase order. It is a pure advisory mandate with no capex or supply content, and at ~1.1% of a Rs 99 cr market cap it sits right on the CLAUDE.md §5 threshold — carried because it clears it, not because the rupees are large.
movers.quantum: Rs 1.05 cr excl GST; ~1.1% of mcap

movers.headline: receives a contract work order for the **supply, installation, testing and commissioning (SITC) of an Access Control System**, valued at **Rs 59,82,402**. The customer is the part the baseline lost to its own truncation: the annexure names it as the **Department of Atomic Energy, Government of India** — a central government security-installation mandate, not the anonymous 'establishment located ....' the RSS subject trailed off into. Sixty lakh rupees is small in absolute terms but it is **~4.5% of a Rs 13 cr market cap**, the smallest listed company on today's mover list by an order of magnitude.

business_updates: **Results season** — **227 companies** filed results or earnings-call material today; tracked in the Results tab. Their rupee figures are revenue and margin numbers, excluded as event amounts by §2.
**Kaynes Technology** — Q1 **revenue Rs 946.0 cr (+40% YoY)** and **EBITDA Rs 147.6 cr (+31%)**.
**Mangalam Worldwide** — **Rs 21.79 cr of export turnover in July** _(~1.7% of mcap; a month of turnover, not a contract)_.
**Tata Technologies** — rumour verification. **IndusInd Bank** — a lifetime-free card with EazyDiner. **LIC** — new product launch. **Rajshree Sugars**, **Sayaji Industries** — operational updates.
capex_core: **Pradeep Metals** — restates its **Rs 250 cr Butibori greenfield project** as an **entry into large-calibre ammunition**, Rs 28.59 cr advanced to 30-Jun; an ongoing project in a results note, not today's approval _(~28% of mcap, the largest capex-to-size ratio on the tape)_.
**Jamna Auto** — **~Rs 47 cr** for a 1,500 MT/month leaf-spring plant at Adityapur under WOS Jai Suspensions, commercial production ~Dec-2027 _(~0.8% of mcap)_.
**Fujiyama Power Systems** — **commissions a 2 GW power-electronics facility at Ratlam**, with 1 GW Mono PERC live and 1.2 GW TOPCon under way; **no rupee investment disclosed**.

**Unvalued or inside a results release (§2):** **Neetu Yoshi** (commercial production begins), **Kalyani Cast-Tech** (Gati Shakti cargo terminal), **The Ramco Cements** (~31 MTPA target FY27, Rs 176 cr Q1 capex), **Cera Sanitaryware**.
**Already published:** **Parag Milk Foods'** Rs 105 cr cheese expansion (60 → 120 MT/day), board-approved 06-Aug.
**Held out — not core capacity:** **JK Tyre** invests ~Rs 1.38 cr for 26% of STTYRE Banmore purely to qualify as a **captive user** of a 6 MWp solar project (§6).
distress_risk: **Bloom Dekor** — approves **promoter reclassification to public** under Reg 31A **and** a **capital reduction and reorganisation**, alongside a resolution plan; none of it quantified — the sharpest distress signal on the tape.

**Sammaan Capital** — NCLT-ordered shareholders' meeting. **Videocon Industries** — Q1 results delayed by an ongoing CIRP. **KSS** — an order dated 05-Aug. **Morgan Ventures** — a board outcome flagged as disagreeing with its subject tag.

**Orders and litigation, none quantified:** **ixigo** (CGST Order-in-Appeal), **Delhivery**, **JSW Dulux**, **Share India Securities**, **Dabur India**, **Vedanta Iron and Steel**, **Nureca**, **DCM**.

**Shankar Lal Rampal Dye-Chem** — document notice. **AVSL Industries** — seized stock and cash recovered. **LT Foods** — a step-down WOS dissolved. **Haryana Financial Corporation** — initial announcement of a **delisting offer**. **C & C Constructions** — its Rs 31 cr / Rs 104 cr figures are 2024 liquidation history, not today's event.
equity_allotments: **Yash Highvoltage (YASHHV)** — **executed**: 12,62,131 shares **and** 8,32,177 warrants at Rs 721, **Rs 151.00 cr in total** — but only the ~Rs 91 cr of shares is capital received now _(~5.5% of mcap)_.
**Tembo Global Industries** — **new warrants**: up to 2,00,00,000 at Rs 57, **up to Rs 114.00 cr**, to promoters and non-promoter investors, pending an EGM _(~10.1% of mcap)_.
**Euro India Fresh Foods** — allots **19,30,000 new warrants at Rs 245, Rs 47.29 cr**, on receipt of 25% — **~Rs 11.82 cr is in, the balance falls due within 18 months** _(~7.1% of mcap)_.
**Utssav CZ Gold Jewels** — **past conversion**: 8,50,000 shares on the balance Rs 166.50 per warrant, **Rs 14.15 cr**; paid-up capital Rs 24.15 → 25.00 cr.
**Kody Technolab** — **past conversion**: 1,23,100 shares at Rs 975 on the balance Rs 731.25, **Rs 9.00 cr**, from Ms. Nikhita Nishid Shah.

**Price not disclosed, so unsizable:** **KIMS** (77,02,182 promoter warrants), **Gretex Corporate Services** (19,51,000 warrants). **Paisalo Digital** — an FCCB conversion (convertible debt). **Balgopal Commercial** — trading approval for 23,38,000 promoter shares.
fund_raises_fresh_equity: **Sangam (India)** — second corrigendum to the 12-Aug EGM notice on **18,00,000 warrants at Rs 555.56, up to Rs 100.00 cr** to promoters, for civil works Rs 25 cr / plant Rs 60 cr / GCP Rs 15 cr by Mar-2029 _(~3.3% of mcap; a corrigendum to a meeting notice, two stages before execution)_.

**Saakshi Medtech** — in-principle approval to issue **20,22,940 shares at Rs 207 to promoters for consideration OTHER than cash** — a share swap for Laxmi Engineering, so **no money is raised** (~Rs 41.9 cr implied, our arithmetic).

**Unquantified process notices:** **Ducon Infratechnologies** (rights issue in-principle), **Sunrest Lifescience** (1:1 rights), **Oriental Rail**, **Koura Fine Diamond**, **Balu Forge**, **Krsnaa Diagnostics**, **Capital India Finance**, **S & T Corporation**.

**Held out as debt (§3):** **Lloyds Metals and Energy** — **Rs 700 cr** of 9.02% senior secured NCDs, 10-year, the day's largest raise; also **Mufin Green** (Rs 50 cr), **Dar Credit** (Rs 15 cr), **Himatsingka Seide** (Rs 5 cr), **RCF** (an NCD interest certificate).
**Held out as ESOP:** **Bandhan Bank**, **AU Small Finance Bank**, **Carborundum Universal**, **CreditAccess Grameen**, **Bharat Wire Ropes**, **Onida Electronics**.
m_and_a: **Bluspring Enterprises** — **completes** the acquisition of **100% of LSG Sky Chefs (India)**; the consideration was disclosed in the April intimation and is **not repeated today**, so it cannot be sized.
**Patil Automation** — buys a further **10% of Mii Robotics, taking it 60% → 70%** in defence automation; the press release discloses no consideration.

**Paras Defence** — approves divesting its entire **47.50% of Krasny Paras** by Dec-2026; the **agreement is unsigned and the consideration expressly not finalised**, and the associate is 0.12% of consolidated turnover.
**Blue Water Logistics** — acquires **47% of its Thai namesake**, 18,800 shares at THB 100 par; **not converted**, and immaterial at par either way.

**No disclosed consideration:** **Texmaco Rail**, **Ugro Capital** (NCLT amalgamation order), **NHPC** (JPCL hearing 25-Aug), **Refex Industries**, **Religare** (demerger update), **Vijaya Diagnostic**, **Lemon Tree**, **Waaree**, **Lancer Container**, **Raymond Realty** (Ten X Mahalaxmi, Rs 1 lakh subscription).
**Already published — cross-day duplicates:** **Chandan Healthcare** Rs 16.77 cr (06-Aug), **SIS** Rs 106 cr and **Industrial Investment Trust** Rs 25 cr (both 05-Aug). Procedure, not news.
order_wins: **Juniper Green Energy** — winning bidder for **230 MW under SECI's 1,000 MW FDRE round-the-clock tender at Rs 5.26/unit**; the **LoA has not been issued**, and no rupee value is disclosed.
**Innomet Advanced Materials** — **Rs 1.09 cr** purchase order from **Federal-Mogul Goetze (India)** _(~0.4% of mcap, under the §5 bar)_.

**RITES** — MoU with **HPCL** for railway-siding consultancy, no consideration disclosed. **Rossell Techsys** — ordinary-course orders, unvalued. **Veljan Denison** — an annual report mis-typed `order_win`.
**Held out — a results PR is never an event amount (§2):** **Interarch** (Rs 1,864 cr order book, a Rs 165 cr Gujarat win during the quarter) and **PPAP Automotive** (~Rs 131 cr of Q1 lifetime wins).
other_notable: **Imagicaaworld** — approves transferring **1,21,00,000 preference shares of Rs 100 face value in JBCG Advisory**; **no consideration stated**, so the Rs 121 cr of face value is not a price.

**Kuber Udyog** (BSE 539408) — public announcement of an **open offer worth Rs 74.65 cr against a Rs 9 cr market cap** — over eight times its own size, but an **acquirer's action on the shares**, never the company's own event.
**Airfloa Rail Technology** — forms a defence/aerospace subsidiary, unquantified.

**Splits, sub-divisions and authorised-capital changes (never movers, §6):** **Spice Islands** (record date), **Aequs** (MOA/AOA), **Koura Fine Diamond** (Rs 7.20 → 7.40 cr), **Jindal Worldwide** (Rs 101 → 146 cr, enabling its rights issue).
**Board outcomes with no quantified event:** **Praruh Technologies**, **Sugs Lloyd**, **Phantom Digital Effects**, **Rama Petrochemicals**, **Jyoti CNC**, **Praxis Home Retail**, **Akshar Spintex**.

**Credit-rating actions — theme-only, never movers (§3):** **JSW Energy** — ICRA assigns **AA-(Stable)/A1+** to the **enhanced** facilities of subsidiary JSW Mahanadi Power, on the day the parent closes a Rs 1,410 cr acquisition.
